discovery-react-vite-zustand: Zustand turns its `devtools` middleware off in production builds (it connects only when `enabled ?? import.meta.env.MODE !== "production"`), so a production build never calls the Redux DevTools API that GenClass listens on, and its stores are not found. The same app with `devtools(..., { enabled: true })` (the `enabled: true` row) is found in every run. Nothing changes for the app either way (every scenario cell is ✓); GenClass then sees the network only. The README now says so; alternatively wrap the store with `genclass` from `@genclass/runtime/zustand`.
next-app-swr-d-observe: A race in the app, not an action: SWR's `rollbackOnError` with two overlapping optimistic mutations (toggle 1 succeeds, toggle 2 fails 120 ms later) sometimes leaves toggle 1 unchecked on screen although the server has it checked. On seed 7 that happened in both runs without GenClass (and in 1 of 2 in an earlier full run the same day), and in none of the 3 runs with GenClass (observe, guard, heal; 6 of 6 across both full runs). GenClass took no action in any of them (one `transient` failure detection, passive decisions only); most likely its own main-thread work (observing the requests, deciding about the HTTP 500 in the background) shifts the timing of SWR's rollback against its revalidation (not traced further). So observe mode is not byte-identical to no GenClass on a racy app: it can change which side of an app's own race wins, here towards the correct outcome. No other observe cell differed in this run.
